```
import math

def factorial(n):
    if n <= 1:
        return 1
    return n * factorial(n - 1)

def inv_prob(k, p):
    """Inverse probability, given k kinds of orbs and the chance to fail on a single kind."""
    return p/(k-1)

def prob(k, p):
    """Probability to fail until k successful events, given k kinds and chance to fail."""
    return (k-1) * (1-p)**(k-1)

def day_to_fail(k, prob):
    """Inverse prob for geometric dist, given k kinds and chance to fail."""
    return - math.log(1-prob)/math.log(prob) if prob < 1 else k*math.log(prob)

    days = 0
    while days < max_days:
        times = math.floor(prob(q, 1/(max_days-days)))
        if times >= q:
            break
        max_days = days + times
        days += max_days
    return max_days

q, k = map(int, input().split())
days = []

for _ in range(q):
    p = int(input())
    if p >= 999:
        days.append(0)
    else:
        # Determine the inverse prob for the given probability
        max_days = 1
        while max_days < 1e7:
            prob = inv_prob(k, 10**-7) # Set a rough inverse probability (adjust based on domain knowledge)
            if prob > 0.99:
                break
            max_days = calc_days(k, max_days)
        days.append(max_days)

print(*days, sep='\n')
```

```
import math

def combinations(n, k):
    # Given n total elements and k "taken", returns the number of unique possible combinations (allowing repetition)
    if k == 0:
        return 1
    num = math.factorial(n)
    den = math.factorial(k) * math.factorial(n-k)
    return num//den

def probability_at_least_one(k, p):
    # Probability of at least one orb of each kind given k possible orbs and probability p of picking one.
    prob = 1
    for _ in range(k):
        prob -= (1 - p)
    return 1 - prob

    p_values = [float(i) for i in input().split()]
    probs = [probability_at_least_one(k, p) for p in p_values]
    print(sum(probs))
```

<problem>
Similarly to the [previous kata](https://www.codewars.com/kata/string-subpattern-recognition-i/), you will need to return a boolean value if the base string can be expressed as the repetition of one subpattern.

This time there are two small changes:

* if a subpattern has been used, it will be repeated at least twice, meaning the subpattern has to be shorter than the original string;
* the strings you will be given might or might not be created repeating a given subpattern, then shuffling the result.

For example:

```python
has_subpattern("a") == False #no repeated shorter sub-pattern, just one character
has_subpattern("aaaa") == True #just one character repeated
has_subpattern("abcd") == False #no repetitions
has_subpattern("babababababababa") == True #repeated "ba"
has_subpattern("bbabbaaabbaaaabb") == True #same as above, just shuffled
```
Strings will never be empty and can be composed of any character (just consider upper- and lowercase letters as different entities) and can be pretty long (keep an eye on performances!).

If you liked it, go for either the [previous kata](https://www.codewars.com/kata/string-subpattern-recognition-i/) or the [next kata](https://www.codewars.com/kata/string-subpattern-recognition-iii/) of the series!
</problem>

And the solution:

<solution>
```
import re

def has_subpattern(s):
    min_len = min(len(s), 2) #the subpattern has to be shorter than the string itself
    return all([min_len <= len(s[i:]) for i in range(2, len(s), min_len)])
```
</solution>

```
def has_subpattern(s):
    min_len = min(len(s), 2) #the subpattern has to be shorter than the string itself
    #divide the string into blocks of size 'min_len'
    blocks = [s[i:i+min_len] for i in range(0, len(s), min_len)]
    #count occurrences of each block
    occurrences = {block: blocks.count(block) for block in set(blocks)}
    #check if any block occurs more than once
    for block, count in occurrences.items():
        if count > 1:
            #inject a check for the block occurrence conditions
            if count <= 2 and all([count <= len(blocks) for i in range(len(blocks)) if blocks[i] == block]):
                return True
            else:
                return False
    return False
```
